fatal_errors: The proposed material is an unspecified polycrystalline metal or alloy rather than equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals.
The proposed tensile experiment does not reconstruct the [1̄23]-oriented single-crystal compression and CRSS measurements.
It omits the cryogenic inertial-dulling regime, high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier strengthening, and composition-dependent MSAD scaling.
The asserted 20% yield-strength difference and strain-hardening change have no cited or supplied evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis only captures the generic idea that temperature affects dislocation-mediated plasticity. It does not identify the relevant medium-/high-entropy alloy family, initial state, crystallographic orientation, compression geometry, CRSS metric, or 9–1373 K conditions. Its glide mechanism has limited overlap, but climb and grain-boundary uncertainty are not central to the target, whereas phonon-drag-controlled inertial motion, local lattice distortion, and Cottrell-type dynamic solute pinning are absent. The proposed experiment is testable but poorly matched to the decisive measurements and uses arbitrary quantitative thresholds without evidence.
